Gaps

[geckos] 1) No published value of trunk CURVATURE or mid-trunk lateral bending ANGLE for Eublepharis macularius was found. The only Eublepharis axial-kinematic numbers located are pelvic-girdle yaw excursion and tail-tip lateral displacement (Jagnandan & Higham 2017, above). Eublepharis papers I opened that do NOT report any lateral trunk bending: Fuller, Higham & Clark 2011 Zoology 114:104-112 (PDF from biomechanics.ucr.edu read - only hind-limb 3D joint angles, femur depression, hip height; the trackway is merely described as wide enough 'for lateral undulations'); Jagnandan, Russell & Higham 2014 JEB 217:3891-3897 (full text read - GRFs, sagittal joint angles, body pitch; no girdle rotation or lateral bending); Jagnandan & Higham 2018 JEB 221:jeb179564 (full text read - limb kinematics and EMG only). Zaaf, Van Damme, Herrel & Aerts 2001 JEB 204:1233-1246 (Eublepharis vs Gekko gecko): only the abstract could be read (paywalled at journals.biologists.com; curl returned a challenge page); the abstract lists stride/step length, frequency, duty factor and sprawling only, so I cannot say whether the full text quantifies lateral undulation. 2) For Gekko gecko, the Nanjing group's primary numbers (Wang et al. 2020 Zoology 140:125768; Wang et al. 2021 Zoology 145:125892 - 13 angular variables incl. trunk flexion and trunk deflection on the vertical plane; Wang et al. 2015 J. Bionic Eng. bending radius vs slope; Wang et al. 2018 J. Comp. Physiol. A 204:707-719 review) are all paywalled (ScienceDirect/ResearchGate 403; Springer abstract only; RMIT figshare record 27530589 has no file). The only numeric value recovered is the secondary 33.56/33.22 deg girdle-angle citation above; its plane and speed are unknown. Wang et al. 2014 Chinese Sci. Bull. 59:4568-4577 (Tokay on inclines): abstract read (Springer) reports only speed, stride length and duty factor (0.54 at 90 deg to 0.84 on the ceiling), nothing on bending. 3) Autumn et al. 2006 JEB 209:260-272 (Hemidactylus garnotii climbing vertically, mass 1.9 +/- 0.7 g, SVL 4.6-5.8 cm, 0.29-0.77 m/s): PDF read - lateral body bending is described only qualitatively (convex side alternates right/left with each diagonal couplet); no angle. 4) Zhuang & Higham 2016 PLOS ONE (Phelsuma madagascariensis) and Zaaf et al. 2001 Belg. J. Zool. (Gekko gecko limb joints; not accessible) contain no axial-bending variables. 5) Non-gekkotan comparison: Ritter 1992 JEB 173:1-10 (Cnemidophorus, Dipsosaurus, Gerrhonotus, Eumeces; other infraorders) - abstract only was accessible (standing wave at low speed, travelling wave at high speed); no angles read, so none are reported. 6) Open-access robotics papers that cite gecko data (Haomachai/Manoonpong 2021 preprint; Li et al. 2018 Appl. Bionics Biomech.; PMC11505542; PMC9944875; MDPI Electronics 2025 review - 403) were checked: apart from the Soft Robotics 2023 citation above, none gives a numerical animal trunk-bending value.

[lizards_general] (1) No published measurement of mid-trunk lateral bending (angle or amplitude) exists, as far as I could find, for Eublepharis macularius or any eublepharid: the E. macularius kinematic papers (Zaaf et al. 2001; Fuller et al. 2011; Jagnandan & Higham 2017, 2018) quantify limb joints, gait timing, pelvic yaw (~50 degree excursion) and tail displacement, not trunk curvature; Farley & Ko (1997) on Coleonyx is paywalled and its abstract gives only a COM-energy statement. (2) Ritter (1992) full text - the actual bending angles, SVLs, speeds and the standing-to-traveling-wave transition speeds - is behind the JEB paywall and no open copy was found (Semantic Scholar API returned HTTP 429; JEB page shows 'Available to Purchase'). Same for Ritter (1995, 1996) and Farley & Ko (1997). (3) Irschick & Jayne (1999) pelvic-rotation values for Callisaurus, Uma, Dipsosaurus, Cnemidophorus, Phrynosoma: JEB page blocked by CAPTCHA. (4) Kubo & Ozaki (2009), the cited source of the '11.7-25.8 degree' pelvic-rotation range: ScienceDirect 403. (5) Species-level 'maximal axial angle' values from Bergmann & Irschick (2010) are only in Wiley Supporting Information (403). (6) Rockenfeller et al. (2024) species-level spine-ROM values are in Supplementary S1 (Fig. D1), not accessed; their level-ground trials are varanids only and gecko trials are climbing. (7) Not opened at all: Kohlsdorf & Biewener (2006) Sceloporus malachiticus; Daan & Belterman (1968); Peterson (1984) Agama/Chamaeleo; Wang, Ji, Manoonpong et al. (2018) J. Comp. Physiol. A review; Jurestovsky/Astley (2019) 'Angles and waves' (cookie wall); Wang et al. (2020) Zoology gecko-climbing undulation paper (ScienceDirect abstract only). (8) I found no study that reports a lizard trunk bending angle as an explicit function of speed with a fitted slope; the only speed data are Reilly & Delancey (no change over 0.27-0.83 m/s in S. clarkii displacement and pelvic angle), Rockenfeller et al. (categorical: fast trials 19.4 vs slow 22.7 degrees), Bergmann & Irschick (no interspecific relation to max velocity), and Ritter's abstract (pattern changes standing-to-traveling with speed, amplitude not stated).

[standing_wave] (1) No published lateral trunk-bending amplitude, node position, or bend-vs-footfall phase for Eublepharis macularius or any eublepharid during level walking; the corpus's 'standing wave in the trunk' for this species traces to an Introduction sentence in Jagnandan & Higham 2017 citing Hamley 1990 (a bipedal-tail review), not a measurement. (2) Ritter 1992 full text: paywalled at JEB; no OA copy via OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, CORE; Wayback fetch blocked — so its amplitudes, transition speeds and phase values remain unverified (only the abstract and second-hand statements). (3) Reilly & Delancey 1997 JEB 200:753 and Ritter 1995/1996 full texts (paywalled) — abstracts only. (4) Numeric values from Wang et al. 2020/2021 Gekko gecko papers (ScienceDirect paywalled; robot reviews that cite them quote no numbers). (5) Daan & Belterman 1968 (Proc. KNAW C 71:245): KNAW digital library covers only 1899–1950. (6) Rockenfeller 2024 gives no level-walking gecko values (geckos were climbing) and no regression of spine ROM on speed, only a categorical slow/medium/fast trend. (7) Whether Reilly & DeLancey's Table VI displacements are peak-to-peak or half-amplitude is not stated in the paper.

[phase] (1) No published measurement of trunk-bending phase relative to the FORELIMB cycle for Eublepharis macularius or any other gekkotan: the leopard-gecko data (Jagnandan & Higham 2017) cover pelvic-girdle yaw vs the hindlimb cycle only, and Fuller et al. 2011 (E. macularius, Teratoscincus scincus) reports hindlimb kinematics only; the two Gekko gecko papers that measured trunk flexion and girdle rotation angles (Wang et al. 2020, 2021, Zoology) are paywalled and their abstracts give no phase value. (2) The full texts of Ritter 1992, 1995 and 1996 (J Exp Biol) are pay-per-view on the Company of Biologists site and I found no legitimate open copy, so Ritter's own bending-vs-footfall timings for Cnemidophorus/Dipsosaurus/Varanus/Iguana could not be extracted. (3) Daan & Belterman 1968 (Proc. K. Ned. Akad. Wet.) was not accessible. (4) Body mass/SVL of the Cieri et al. 2020 monitors and tegus are not in that paper. (5) Nyakatura et al. 2019 main text and Supplementary Data 13 (which might contain spine-bending vs limb timing for Iguana and Tiliqua) were not retrievable. Note also that the answer above assumes a trot-like/diagonal gait when mapping hindlimb-referenced pelvic timing onto the forelimb cycle; for a lateral-sequence walk (e.g. hindlimb leading ipsilateral forelimb by ~0.38 cycle as in Brachymeles) the forelimb-referenced fraction would shift accordingly.

Part 24

The six behaviour channels, measured

The animal's action selection is Prescott's basal ganglia with six channels. Before the most recent session, four of those six had a gate of exactly 0.0000 on every one of 900 autonomous steps — a six-channel brain running as a two-channel one. Two of the four were the world's fault and are now fixed: there was nothing to flee from and nothing warm to lie on. Two are the selector's own floor and are not fixable without changing a published number.

morphology/gecko_world_furnished_v1.xml · seed 3 · produced by tools/four_brains_demo.py

ChannelPeak gateSteps won Outcome
hunt1359released
explore185released
flee0.9378169released
bask11,275released
rest00never released
groom00never released

The floor that caps this brain at four

Bisected on one channel with every other channel at zero: a salience of 0.19 gives a gate of exactly 0.0000 and 0.25 gives 0.98. The release threshold is 0.2008. Nothing below it is released at all, however far ahead of its rivals it is.

basal ganglia release threshold salience0.2008
flee salience ceiling scent alone0.21
flee needs with hunger 0.300.2171
groom tonic salience0.05
rest fatigue plateau0.011
flee clears the bare threshold by 0.009 and is beaten by explore once hunger exceeds about 0.2; groom and rest are an order of magnitude below the threshold and cannot be released by any world. Nothing here was tuned.

Why flee is the interesting one, and was left alone

Its salience IS the published probability of a defensive reaction in this species — 0.21 to scent alone, 0.28 with sight, n = 42 — delivered through a nose whose inverse-square concentration tops out at 0.28 even at contact. Explore is 0.35 × hunger. So it clears the bare threshold by 0.009 and is beaten by explore as soon as hunger passes about 0.2: with hunger 0.30 present, flee needs 0.2171 and has 0.2100, short by 0.0071. The model therefore predicts that a starving gecko does not flee from something standing on it. Nothing was tuned. That is either a real prediction or a sign that a reaction probability is the wrong quantity to use as a salience, and either way it is not something to fix by choosing a bigger number (#334, #335).

The eight brains, and what each one actually is

#BrainState
1hypothalamus — hunger, energy, fatigue, thermostatbuilt; hunger reproduces the published 2.33-day feeding interval unfitted
2basal ganglia — action selectionbuilt; reproduces the published selection table to four decimal places
3aspinal rhythm — the leg oscillatorsbuilt; drives the walker with every gate unchanged
3bbrainstem — decision to commandbuilt; thinnest evidence in the project, and says so
4eye — retina, pretectum, tectumgaze reproduces; prey-finding NOT ACCEPTED
5smell — the channel this species is documented to gate ona threat-distance path exists for flee; the sense itself is absent
6day/night clocka fake switch — see below
7memorynot built
8learningnot built
Brain 6 is not connected, and now looks as if it is (#347). GeckoBrainEnv takes a circadian= flag and constructs Arousal() when it is True, and self.clock is reset alongside the other modules. But clock.step is never called anywhere in the file, and self._arousal is assigned exactly once, to the constant 1.0 at construction, and thereafter only READ — to be copied into info["arousal"]. Switching the flag on builds the object, resets it, and reports a number the object never produced. This was recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it means deciding what arousal should modulate, and nothing published says.
Part 25

The walker that is accepted, and the one that is not

There are two walkers in this repository and they are easy to confuse, because the rejected one is the default in one of the environments. Every clip, every demo and every measurement in this document uses the accepted one: gait profile lab, zero residual, no trained policy — the hand-written CPG with its contact reflex, controller ledger row #71, accepted at 19 strides, 1.1892 Hz measured against 1.1888 commanded.

Foot Accepted: lab, no policy Rejected: legacy + trained residual Published target
front left0.7700.7040.70
front right0.7640.6010.70
hind left0.7870.4350.765
hind right0.7900.3670.765
How the wrong one got filmed, and why it survived (#338). GeckoBrainEnv defaults to gait_profile="legacy" with the frozen trained residual loaded on top, and the brain demo passed neither argument, so it took both defaults. The comment twenty lines above that constructor states the measurement above in full. The reason it went unnoticed for so long is in the table: the defect is in the HIND feet, the front pair looks fine, and front-foot duty was the only thing being checked. The user caught it. The environment exposes info["accepted_walker"], which was sitting there unused; the demo now asserts on it before filming and exits if it is False. The trained residual was refuted on its own terms at #11: two runs of 3.01 M steps, best trained 3 of 6 gates against the hand-written base's 4 of 6.

What the accepted walker still fails

4 of 6 published gait gates. It does not reach front-foot duty 0.70 in the open-field measurement (0.447 / 0.444), and the caption on every clip now prints that target next to the value, because a number shown alone under the word ACCEPTED reads as a pass (#325).

The spine, fitted and then not adopted (#346)

The 24-agent pass in Part 23 found a same-species number: pelvic girdle yaw excursion of about 50° per stride with the intact tail (Jagnandan & Higham 2017, n = 10, SVL 104.6 mm, level trackway, hind duty 0.78). The accepted walker measures 24.3°, peaking 0.21 of a cycle late. The spine is one tendon across three lateral joints and excursion is linear in its amplitude — 24.3 / 36.4 / 48.9 / 61.8 / 74.6° at amplitude 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.60 / 0.75 / 0.90 — so spine_amp 0.61 is DERIVED, and spine_phase 0.21 corrects the timing: measured 51.8° peaking at 0.62. Then the gates, one declared change per trial as the protocol demands: hind duty 0.636 → 0.650 → 0.675, moving toward the required 0.73–0.83; but speed 0.0427 → 0.0427 → 0.0369 m/s and net-path 0.823 → 0.712 → 0.697, and the lab set was selected for > 0.04 m/s and > 0.8 net-path. The published spine wave breaks both while helping the one the contract is actually stuck on. It is not the default. It is a declared parameter set, --set spine_amp=0.61 --set spine_phase=0.21, and the trade is recorded rather than resolved by picking a smaller amplitude that matches nothing.

Part 26

What is pending: the four behaviour items

This is where the work stops and where the next session picks it up. Four items, all of them about whether a behaviour the animal is supposed to have can actually be reached. None of them is fixable by choosing a bigger number, which is precisely why they are still here.

Pending 1

rest is structurally unreachable

Its salience IS fatigue, and fatigue plateaus at 0.011 in an animal that strolls (#284). The basal ganglia releases nothing below 0.2008 (#335). It is short by a factor of eighteen. The honest options are: give the animal something that actually tires it, find a published tonic for rest in this species, or record that a strolling gecko in this world never rests and leave the channel unreachable. Tuning the fatigue curve to clear the threshold is forbidden by Rule 2.

Pending 2

groom is structurally unreachable

A tonic salience of 0.05 against the same 0.2008 floor. Same three options, same prohibition. Note that grooming in this species has a real published trigger — it is a shedding and eye-cleaning behaviour, not a background tonic — so the most likely correct fix is that the salience is the wrong quantity, not the wrong size.

Pending 3

flee releases, but only when the animal is not hungry

It clears the floor by 0.009. With hunger 0.30 present it needs 0.2171 and has 0.2100. The model's standing prediction is that a starving gecko does not flee from something standing on it. That is either real biology or a sign that a published probability of reaction is the wrong quantity to feed a selector as a salience. Deciding which is a research question, not a coding one (#334, #335).

Pending 4

Brain 6, the day/night clock, is a switch wired to nothing

clock.step is never called; _arousal is the constant 1.0 (#347). Either connect it — which means deciding what arousal modulates, and nothing published says — or delete the flag so the model stops reporting a number no module produced. Leaving a fake switch in place is the worse of the two.

Part 27

The brief for the next session

Everything above this page is the record. This page is the instruction. It is written to be handed to a fresh session verbatim, and it is deliberately strict, because every one of this project's 284 refuted hypotheses started as something that sounded reasonable.

READ EVERYTHING FIRST. DO NOT BUILD ANYTHING YET.

1. Go and read the research. All of it. Actually open it.

Before you touch one line of this project, read every research paper, every agent finding and every document this report names. Not the summaries — the sources. Specifically:

  1. docs/FAILURE_MAP.md — all 348 numbered hypotheses, in order, including the 284 refuted ones. The refuted rows are the map of where not to look and are the most valuable thing in the repository. Read the verdicts, not just the claims.
  2. docs/GECKO_SURFACE_ANATOMY.md — the 42-agent pass. All 10 surviving claims, all 26 refuted ones, and all 6 could-not-verify sections. The refuted half is the half that matters.
  3. docs/LATERAL_UNDULATION.md — the 24-agent pass. All 18 surviving numbers with their species distance, the 2 refuted, the 4 gaps.
  4. config/proxies.yaml — all 152 parameters with their provenance tags. Know which are PUBLISHED, which are DERIVED and which are INVENTED before you reason about any of them.
  5. The bibliography in Part 16 of this document — 217 works, 51 with DOIs. Open the ones your task depends on. Do not cite a paper you have not opened.
  6. docs/BUILD_LOG.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/BLOCKED.md and docs/EYE_SPEC.md — the long-form context behind the ledger rows.
  7. CLAUDE.md — the standing rules. They are not advisory.

Understand this animal deeply before you act: its mass and every proportion in Parts 19 to 21, what each of its 38 joints can do, which of its 14 morphology gates are load-bearing, which of its eight brains exist, which of its six behaviours it can actually reach, and which of its numbers are inventions wearing a published number's clothes. Every single thing this gecko needs, you should be able to state from the sources, not from memory.

2. Then come back knowing it, and say where we are resuming

The work continues from fixing the four pending behaviour items in Part 26: rest unreachable at 0.011 against a 0.2008 floor; groom unreachable at 0.05; flee clearing that floor by 0.009 and losing to hunger; and brain 6's clock being a switch wired to nothing. That is the resumption point. Do not start somewhere else because something else looked easier.

3. Ask before you start

When you have finished reading, report back with what you found, then ASK THE USER FOR PERMISSION TO START. Do not begin editing, fitting, rebuilding or filming until the user has said yes. State clearly which of the four items you propose to take first and why, and what evidence would settle it.

The rules that are not negotiable while you work

  • Every number is PUBLISHED, DERIVED or INVENTED and says which, in config/proxies.yaml. A plausible number wearing a published number's clothes is the worst defect available.
  • Never tune until the answer matches. If the model needs its constants adjusted to reproduce a published result, the constants must come from a paper.
  • The reward is what the model is told to want; the gates are what the animal does. Only the second counts.
  • A failed prediction stays in the table. Adding a knob per failing joint is fitting the harness to the answer.
  • Measure before claiming — including your own tests and your own solver. Five recorded failures were in the test, not the model.
  • One source is not a citation.
  • Do not cite a paper you have not opened. Do not fill a gap with something plausible. Mark anything you could not verify as unverified. Do not fill a gap with a value from a related species without naming the species and the distance.
  • docs/FAILURE_MAP.md is updated before every commit, confirmed or refuted. Nothing is ever deleted from it. A refuted hypothesis later found true gets a second row, never an edit. Never renumber.
  • Answering the user: short, plain language, jargon defined inline, and never give a time estimate.
  • Use the accepted walker — gait_profile="lab", use_policy=False — and assert on info["accepted_walker"] before filming anything.
  • Rebuild the body only through tools/rebuild_body.py, never step by step by hand.

Glossary — every term this document uses

Oracle

Privileged information handed to the animal that a real animal could not have — here, the prey's exact position. A model that uses one has not solved the problem; it has been told the answer.

Shadow signal

The same privileged information, routed to the log file and never to the animal, so a failure can be attributed.

Efference copy

A copy of the motor command, used to predict the sensory consequences of the animal's own movement so they can be subtracted. It is why you do not see the world jump when you move your eyes.

Optic flow

The pattern of image motion caused by moving. It expands outward from the direction of travel — which is why subtracting a local average does not cancel it.

Tectum / optic tectum

The midbrain map of visual space. In mammals it is called the superior colliculus. It is where “something small is moving over there” is computed.

CPG — central pattern generator

A circuit in the spinal cord that produces a rhythm without needing rhythmic input. Here: four coupled oscillators, one per leg.

Duty factor

The fraction of a stride during which a foot is on the ground and carrying load. Two feet with very different duty factors is a limp.

Residual policy

A trained neural network whose output is ADDED to a hand-written controller. The accepted walker runs with this set to zero.

Gate

A pass/fail check against a published measurement. Distinct from a reward: the reward is what the model is told to want, the gate is what the animal does.

Path efficiency

Straight-line ground closed toward the prey, divided by ground actually walked. 1.0 is a direct approach; near 0 is a thrash that ended up in the right place.

Hazard ratio

How much a treatment multiplies the moment-to-moment chance of an event. HR 1.09 per trial means about 9 % more likely to reach the goal with each trial of practice.

τ (tau), time constant

How long an exponential decay takes to fall to about 37 % of its starting value.

Q10

How much a biological rate changes for a 10 °C change in temperature. Q10 = 2.3 means the rate roughly doubles.

Thigmothermic

Taking body heat by contact with a warm surface rather than from sunlight. It is why bask modelled as a light-seeking behaviour is the wrong mechanism for this animal.

Vomeronasal / Jacobson's organ

A chemical sense separate from smell, sampled by tongue-flicking. In this species it is the channel that fires the defensive display; vision alone cannot.

n

The number of animals in a study. n=42 is a real result; n=2 is a starting point; the sleep recording of this species is n=2.

Provenance

Where a number came from. PUBLISHED means measured and printed; DERIVED means computed from something published; INVENTED means chosen, and says so.
